data.title: BNPL Spending Step-Up to Limit Bust-Out Pattern
data.description: Detects the characteristic spending escalation pattern of BNPL bust-out fraud, where accounts begin with small purchases (under $50) during a credit grooming phase, then rapidly escalate to purchases consuming 85% or more of the available credit limit within 14 days. This pattern distinguishes synthetic bust-out operations from legitimate consumer behavior, where spending typically ramps gradually over weeks to months. Recorded in organized rings deploying 50-1,000+ synthetic identities, the grooming-to-bustout transition represents the highest-confidence detection window for TP-0040 Phase 4 execution, as the sharp behavioral shift from conservative to aggressive spending is difficult for fraudsters to avoid without sacrificing the speed required for coordinated multi-provider bust-out.

detection.condition: selection and filter_first_order and filter_limit_usage and filter_timespan

falsepositives: Legitimate consumers building confidence with a new BNPL provider before making a planned large purchase
Seasonal shopping patterns where consumers save large purchases for sales events
